theorem_obligations.intent: For fixed pre-state and instruction, a `ShlB32Step` has at most one post-state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If `ShlB32Step s i s1` and `ShlB32Step s i s2`, then `s1 = s2`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem ShlB32_ShlB32Step_deterministic (s : MachineState) (i : ShlB32Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState) (h1 : ShlB32Step s i s1) (h2 : ShlB32Step s i s2) : s1 = s2
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The relation includes both `guardFalse` and `executed` constructors; equality is not by reflexivity because guard cases and source-read-dependent updates both matter.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case split on h1/h2 by constructors. Mismatch of constructors gives contradiction from distinct evalGuard requirements; matching constructors reduce to congruence of identical `updateDestination` states.

theorem_obligations.intent: Align `execShlB32` and `ShlB32Step` for both executed/guard-false branches and for no-step/pure none behavior.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) `execShlB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')` iff `ShlB32Step s i s'`; (b) `execShlB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')` iff `ShlB32Step s i s'`; (c) `execShlB32 s i = none` iff there is no `s'` with `ShlB32Step s i s'`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem ShlB32_execShlB32_iff_step (s : MachineState) (i : ShlB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) : execShlB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ↔ ShlB32Step s i s'
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Executed/guard-false and none cases are in exact correspondence between function and relation.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Both sides are partial and include multiple branch constructors; proving equivalence tests that mapping did not drop/forge branches.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold definitions and split on `evalGuard`; for each branch match against constructors of the relation and use `readSource` cases to build equivalence. For `none`, show failure iff neither relation constructor is constructible.

theorem_obligations.intent: On true predicate with resolved operands, the destination register write equals `shlValue va vb`.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If `evalGuard s i.guard = some true`, `i.d = Destination.reg r`, and both source reads succeed with `va` and `vb`, then the executed post-state writes `shlValue va vb` into `r`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem ShlB32_execShlB32_writes_shift_result (s : MachineState) (i : ShlB32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : B32) (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) (ha : readSource s i.a = some va) (hb : readSource s i.b = some vb) : ∃ s', execShlB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ∧ s'.valueRegs r = some (shlValue va vb)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
ha : readSource s i.a = some va
hb : readSource s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: The executed destination value is exactly `shlValue va vb`.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: This theorem fixes the computed register value, proving the core dataflow formula rather than merely asserting control-flow branches.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: From hguard and `ha/hb`, unfold `execShlB32` to the executed branch and simplify `updateDestination` at reg `r` using `hd`.

theorem_obligations.intent: A false complete guard causes the no-op behavior in both executable and relational forms.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If `evalGuard s i.guard = some false`, then `execShlB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s)`; and any step `ShlB32Step s i s'` under this guard is forced to `s' = s`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem ShlB32_false_guard_no_state_change (s : MachineState) (i : ShlB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) (hstep : ShlB32Step s i s') : execShlB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s) ∧ s' = s
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false
theorem_obligations.conclusion: False guard is a true no-op on state in this bounded model.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Guard-false branches are reachable and distinct in bounded semantics; this excludes accidental writes when predicate is false.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold `evalGuard`/`execShlB32`; use contradiction on executed constructor (requires true guard) and derive reflexive state equality from `guardFalse` constructor.
